questions.question: Emergency roof hatches on a bus:

options.text: Must be closed before the bus is driven.
Can be opened to let in fresh air while driving.
Must be removed before the bus is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be opened to let in fresh air while driving.
questions.explanation: Some emergency roof hatches can be locked open to let in fresh air. Do not do this regularly.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Leave more space between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between your car and the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance to the car ahead. This reduces the need for sudden speed or direction changes and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: When you apply the brakes, your vehicle should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not pull to either side.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, it may mean your brakes are not working properly.

questions.question: People working on a broken-down vehicle:

options.text: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
Do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a broken-down vehicle. They may be focused on fixing the car and not paying attention to traffic.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, look ahead about ____ .
questions.correctAnswerText: A quarter mile
questions.explanation: Watch at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead on the road to see upcoming hazards. At highway speeds, this is about a quarter mile.

questions.question: When checking the inside of a bus, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Test every railing.
questions.explanation: When checking a bus inside, make sure everything is safe and working. Check that each railing and handhold is secure and safe to use.

questions.question: When are people usually least alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Tired driving crashes happen more often at night than any other time.

questions.question: In wet conditions, if other vehicles are not spraying water from their tires, it means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is stuck under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, no spray from tires means ice is on the road. Be extra careful when driving in wet, cold weather.

questions.question: Aggressive driving is:

options.text: Driving in a rude or pushy way.
Driving with concern for other drivers' safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a rude or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving is driving in a rude or pushy way without caring about the safety of other drivers and road users.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: When passing a driver, cyclist, or pedestrian, assume they do not see you. This is a safe driving practice.

questions.question: Traction is important for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Safe braking.
questions.explanation: Without good traction, you cannot brake or steer your vehicle safely. Always check that your tires are in good condition before you drive.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect your braking distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples.
questions.explanation: Doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph makes your braking distance four times longer, not just twice as long. Higher speeds mean longer braking distances.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern since it is stopped.
Only a concern if you see passengers getting off.
Always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful near a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby, and the bus could block your view or theirs. A stopped bus is always a safety concern.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes before slowing down. This makes your brake lights flash, which warns drivers behind you.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, the warning lights and buzzers should turn on briefly, then turn off right away.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Keep the air cool by using the air conditioner or opening a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the air cool by using the air conditioner or opening a window.
questions.explanation: To avoid getting tired while driving, keep the air cool with the air conditioner or open window. Avoid heavy foods and take rest breaks every two hours or every 100 miles.

questions.question: Refueling a bus in an enclosed space, towing a bus with passengers, and talking to passengers are considered:
questions.correctAnswerText: Prohibited practices.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must not talk to passengers, fuel a bus inside a building, or tow a bus with passengers aboard. These are all prohibited.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must:

options.text: Explain what you are checking and why.
Guess the weight of a trailer load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a full inspection of your vehicle. You must tell the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: Passengers cannot stand in front of the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Standee line.
questions.explanation: On a bus with standing passengers, no one may stand in front of the driver's seat. Buses must have a line on the floor showing where passengers cannot stand. This is called the standee line.

questions.question: When making tight turns or maneuvers, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door to see better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use their mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. Always check your mirrors carefully when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers.
